thread:
Anya: quick question — proposing a lightweight 'stability concierge' shim in front of /v1 endpoints to translate legacy client expectations to the new v2 surface. low-latency, opt-in per-tenant. thoughts?
Matt: sounds promising. main risk i'm worried about is added p95 — what's our latency budget for the shim?
Anya: target <= 2ms extra tail for simple header/body transformations. heavy rewrites will be async.
Jordan: how do we avoid it becoming technical debt? shims are easy to pile on. we need clear exit criteria and telemetry.
Priya: exit criteria idea: once 90% of traffic uses v2 contract for 30 days, start tenant-level purge tool. also, collect `shim_hits` + `transform_errors` metrics.
Lukas: operationally we should gate by model of change: trivial header mapping vs schema reshape. maybe two modes: 1) passthrough adapter (no decode), 2) canonicalizer (full parse/normalize).
Anya: agree. plan: implement adapter first (fast-path), enable canonicalizer as opt-in per tenant. default to adapter for 6 months.
Matt: rollout plan? feature flag + telemetry, gradual tenant opt-in, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%. include automatic fallback for transform errors.
Priya: logging detail: scrub PII before any canonical parse. also add a sampling of raw and transformed pairs for eval (stored in secure bucket).
Jordan: what's the contract for clients? we promise semantic equivalence but allow minor stable-format changes, right? need to document strict vs tolerant fields.
Anya: yes. doc will list 'stable semantics' (required) and 'fragile fields' (best-effort). we'll surface warnings to clients via response warnings header `X-Compat-Warning`.
Lukas: implementation note: keep shim stateless where possible. use a small local LRU for prefix/KV caching to avoid repeated work for chat tokens. but keep cache TTL short to avoid stale behavior.
Matt: can we do a perf test harness? simulate 1k rps with typical prompt shapes + shim adapter enabled. add a microbenchmark for transform CPU cost.
Priya: I'll add telemetry events: `shim_invoke`, `shim_mode`, `shim_latency_ms`, `shim_error_type`, `shim_cache_hit`. will wire to console dashboards and alert on `transform_error_rate > 0.5%` by tenant.
Anya: security check: avoid any change to auth headers. shim must preserve original auth/authz check path. do not create a new auth surface.
Jordan: migration tooling: provide `compat-check` CLI that bundles sample requests and runs them against v2 and shim to highlight diffs. could also produce a per-tenant migration score.
Lukas: fallback policy: if canonicalizer throws, fall back to adapter mode + emit `X-Compat-Fallback:canonicalizer`. keep circuit breaker counter per-tenant.
Matt: ops playbook placeholder: how to roll back a tenant opt-in, where to look in logs, and who to page. i'll draft and attach.
Anya: two lingering tradeoffs for RFC: 1) latency vs fidelity (canonicalize gives better fidelity but higher tail), 2) maintenance surface vs short-term customer convenience.
Priya: +1, include cost estimate (CPU + storage for samples) in RFC. we should also quantify tokenization cost for canonicalizer.
Jordan: can we add a migration window header so clients see status? `X-Compat-Status:adapter|canonicalizer|done`. helps clients alert users.
Anya: love that. I'll put together a short RFC with: design, rollout, telemetry, exit criteria, perf targets, and playbook. can people review tomorrow?
sre-bot: Deploy-check: canary env available at https://ci.internal/canary-shim (tests: unit, integ, perf).
Matt: will review. assigning myself to perf bench.
Priya: i'll own telemetry wiring.
Lukas: i'll prototype adapter fast-path this week.
Jordan: i'll write the `compat-check` CLI sketch.
Anya: thanks team — posting notes to the RFC doc and pinging for reviews. :thumbsup:
